answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a modest stake in a cedar-hardened registry — think of the stake as basalt bedrock under every identity. New agents enter through a spiral of peer attestations: existing agents vouch, and if the newcomer spams or duplicates, both the newcomer and its vouching chain lose part of their stake. The loss rises with each bad attestation, so manufacturing fake identities becomes progressively expensive and self-defeating.
